column1: # *** TWO THINGS THE CENSUSES SETTLED THAT A TREE HAD LEFT WRONG OR BLANK - 14 September 2026 ***
*** ARE KATHLEEN GEORGINA AND WILLIAM JOHN TWINS? *** This archive's own note said "same birth month as Kathleen - twins, or one date is wrong", and left it
column2: *** THE 1871 CENSUS HAS BOTH INFANTS IN THE HOUSE. *** "William J Taylor, b.1871 Bideford, parents Mary A H Taylor and William Taylor, siblings Kathleen G Taylor" - taken 2 April 1871. Their parents' BANNS were called at Bideford on *** 9 JANUARY 1870 ***, so the first possible child is late 1870
column3: *** TWINS, born NOVEMBER 1870. *** It is the only reading left. Two children of one mother, both alive in the house in April 1871, cannot be separate births when the marriage is fifteen months old. *** SO THE FAMILY HAD TWO SETS OF TWINS - Kathleen and William John in 1870, and Irene and her unnamed sister in 1879. ***

column1: *** WHOM DID WILLIAM JOHN MARRY? *** The tree says "Fanny Ellen JEFFEREY (1870-1944)"; this archive could find no such marriage
column2: *** THE CENSUSES NAME HER FANNY HELEN. *** 1901, Northam: "William John Taylor, b.1871 Bideford, spouse FANNY HELEN TAYLOR, children GLADYS HELEN and WILLIAM ARCHIBALD." 1911, *** PAIGNTON: *** "William Taylor, b.1871 Bideford, *** married 1892 ***, spouse Fanny, children Gladys and William"
column3: *** MARRIED IN 1892, TO A FANNY HELEN. *** The marriage act itself is still not found and the surname JEFFEREY is still unsupported by any record. What is now documented is the date, the wife's forenames and two children.

column1: *** WHERE DID "JEFFEREY" COME FROM? *** - asked because a wrong name is worse than a blank
column2: The ONLY marriage of a Fanny Jeffreys to a Taylor in England is *** JAMES WILLIAM TAYLOR to FANNY JEFFREYS, 27 May 1893, St John, Dukinfield, CHESHIRE *** - father John Taylor
column3: *** A LIKELY TREE CONFLATION, stated as a suspicion and not as a finding. *** Same decade, similar name, different man, different county, different father. This archive cannot prove the tree took it from there. It can say that no Devon record supports JEFFEREY, that the censuses say HELEN, and that a Cheshire marriage of almost the same shape exists.

column1: # ================ *** AND A GEOGRAPHY NOBODY HERE HAD NOTICED *** ================
# In 1911 WILLIAM JOHN TAYLOR is at *** PAIGNTON *** in south Devon. In 1909 his sister LUCY ELIZABETH had
# her banns called at *** CHURSTON FERRERS *** - the next parish but one, three miles down the same coast,
# and eighty miles from Northam where they were both born.
# *** SO TWO OF THE TEN LEFT NORTH DEVON FOR THE SAME CORNER OF SOUTH DEVON, and the brother was there
# first. *** Lucy almost certainly followed him. It is the same shape as the thing this archive keeps
# finding in Montevideo - that people do not move at random, they move to where a relative already is -
# and it is the first time the Taylor side has shown it.
# THE SAME HABIT SHOWS IN THE NAMES. *** WILLIAM ARCHIBALD TAYLOR (1893) and HORACE HENRY CHARLES DALLING
# (c.1901) both carry HORACE ARCHIBALD TAYLOR'S names *** - an uncle honoured twice in two households; and
# RONALD WILLIAM JAMES DALLING carries his grandfather William's. *** This is the naming discipline this
# archive already documented on the Lerena side, where Pablo Armando's eldest son was RICARDO JUAN CARLOS
# for the grandfather nobody can find. It runs on the Devon side too. ***
